title: Barry Marshall & Robin Warren (1951– / 1937–2024) — Helicobacter pylori, Self-Infection & the 2005 Nobel

teenKit.tldr: When the medical establishment refused to believe that bacteria could survive the deadly acid of the human stomach and cause ulcers, scientist Barry Marshall swallowed a billion live germs to prove them wrong.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This radical act of self-experimentation completely upended decades of false medical dogma, turning painful, lifelong ulcers from a chronic mystery into a condition easily cured with a simple round of antibiotics.
keyTakeaways: Entrenched institutions and expert guilds often reject paradigm-shifting truths to protect their own status and standard practices.
Peripheral freedom and cross-disciplinary thinking allow researchers to see patterns that insiders blinded by dogma completely miss.
Theatrical self-experimentation can bypass bureaucratic red tape and force a stubborn establishment to pay attention to undeniable physical reality.

vocab.meaning: Inflammation of the protective lining of the stomach that causes chronic pain, nausea, and burning.
A painful sore that develops on the inside lining of the stomach or the upper part of the small intestine.
A rigid set of scientific rules used to prove that a specific microbe is the direct cause of a specific disease.
The tactical use of leverage, timing, and bold presentation to force new and disruptive ideas into a resistant culture.

quiz.question: Why did Barry Marshall have to drink a beaker of bacteria in secret instead of getting official approval?
options: He forgot to fill out the digital safety forms before the lab closed.
Hospital ethics boards and senior surgeons would have blocked the experiment immediately.
He wanted to shoot a viral video for a medical documentary series.
The hospital's ethics committee was on holiday in the southern hemisphere winter.
quiz.explanation: Because the medical establishment was totally convinced no bacteria could survive stomach acid, any official board would have rejected his dangerous proposal instantly.

quiz.question: What was the textbook medical belief about stomach ulcers before Marshall and Warren's discovery?
options: They were caused exclusively by stress, spicy foods, and excess stomach acid.
They were genetic mutations passed down through families.
They were viral infections caught from drinking contaminated water supplies.
They were purely psychosomatic illnesses with no physical root cause.
quiz.explanation: Doctors firmly believed that stress and acid were the culprits, treating ulcers with lifelong diets and antacids rather than looking for living pathogens.

quiz.question: What real-world impact did proving the existence of Helicobacter pylori ultimately have on medicine?
options: It led to the invention of expensive lifelong surgeries for ulcer patients.
It proved that stomach acid is actually generated by foreign microbes.
It turned a chronic, lifelong disease into an easily curable condition using cheap antibiotics.
It forced hospitals to ban all human self-experimentation worldwide.
quiz.explanation: By identifying a bacteria as the root cause, doctors could finally kill the infection with antibiotics instead of just treating the symptoms.
